args.text: When the process description specifies multiple activities that must all be completed, model them as parallel branches and synchronize them with a parallel gateway; distinguish these from alternatives or conditional outcomes.

trace.reason: Check existing documented guidance on parallel branches, joins, and choices before proposing a guideline.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.

result.rule: When the description identifies mutually exclusive outcomes for a process decision.: Model an exclusive decision gateway with a separate outgoing path for each stated outcome, and ensure each path reaches its appropriate terminal outcome.

When the description states that a process can end in two or more mutually exclusive outcomes: Model each outcome on its own branch from a decision gateway, connecting that branch to the corresponding outcome activity or end event.

When the description states that an activity follows another only after a condition or approval is met: Model the stated order with sequence flows, and use a decision gateway before the dependent activity to route the outcomes that the description specifies.

When the description states that an observed value is assessed against a stated limit and that the result determines whether a subsequent response is needed.: Model the assessment after the activity that observes the value as a decision gateway, with outgoing paths for the outcomes stated in the description, and route each response only along its applicable outcome.

args.text: When labeling BPMN tasks and events, use concise labels that faithfully reflect the actions and outcomes stated in the process description, avoiding invented or contradictory meanings.

trace.reason: Check existing documented guidance on faithful BPMN labels before proposing a guideline.

result.rule: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Create reusable bpmn:message elements and messageRef only when communication content or shared message identity matters.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

args.text: When labeling BPMN tasks and events, use concise labels that faithfully reflect the actions and outcomes stated in the process description, avoiding invented or contradictory meanings.

trace.reason: Check whether an already learned guideline covers the label-faithfulness issue.

result.rule: When the description states an activity together with a purpose, object, or scope that distinguishes what is being done: Label the corresponding BPMN task with its core action and enough of those stated details to preserve the activity’s meaning; do not add unsupported details or omit details that distinguish it.

When the description gives an activity together with contextual or implementation details: label the corresponding BPMN element with its core action and object, omitting details that do not distinguish the activity.
When the description states how the process begins or ends: Label the corresponding start and end events with the described trigger or outcome rather than generic labels.

When the description says that a broader process stage begins and names activities included in it: Label the corresponding BPMN activity to express the start of that stage; do not label it as performing or finishing one of the included activities unless the description says so.
